text: Nix/Home Manager ownership is separated from linker ownership.
Filesystem layout is the linker contract instead of a link manifest.
Link replacement and pruning are opt-in and ledger-bound.
Work-profile state is outside managed files.
Primary user-facing contracts are CLI tools, Nix outputs, and file conventions.
Home-sync is a Click command group for sync, daemon, status, and version operations.
The linker fails collisions by default and requires explicit replacement confirmation.
Nix activation, Zsh compilation, and locked npm synchronization are supported build-like processes.
Legacy installation remains supported alongside the Nix path.
CI covers quality gates, Nix evaluation, installation, and Python validation.
CI runs only two maintained Bats integration suites.
Documentation link checking and TODO reporting are non-blocking.
The flake constructs standalone Home Manager and nix-darwin configurations from a shared module.
Home Manager owns declared shell, Git, and agent-instruction files and migrates known legacy links.
The convention linker owns unmanaged home files and public commands with a safe ledger lifecycle.
Zsh startup reads mutable environment state that work-mode writes atomically with mode 0600.
Install defaults to user activation and makes nix-darwin system activation opt-in.
Installed machine state and live external availability are outside the snapshot.
Repository source configuration is version-controlled and Home Manager materializes declared home files.
Link ownership records live at an uncommitted XDG state path.
Work-mode state is mutable and local.
No database schema or networked persistent data store was identified.
Nix configuration drives Home Manager/nix-darwin and scripts depend outward on local tools.
The linker excludes Home Manager-owned targets.
No repository-wide architectural dependency-rule checker was found.
Standalone Home Manager is the default deployment and nix-darwin is opt-in with rollback support.
A LaunchAgent can run home-sync at login and on an interval.
The Nix path configures host identity, activates Nix tooling, syncs npm tools, and compiles Zsh; a legacy path remains.
Linker apply validates a plan before mutation and records completed ownership state.
Home-sync validates, optionally commits, fast-forward pulls, and pushes inside a savepoint.
The repository is workstation infrastructure with optional local launchd automation.
No cloud infrastructure, container orchestration, or service discovery was found.
Activation integrates Nix, Home Manager, nix-darwin, and declared Homebrew exceptions.
Sync uses Git remotes and credential tools use Keychain and encrypted stores.
CI uploads Python coverage to Codecov.
The README documents focused validation commands for Nix, scripts, integration, and Python work.
Home-sync daemon performs periodic local work and is deployable through launchd.
Force sync stages all changes and rollback can reset and clean a repository.
Home-sync CLI configuration is not evidenced as wired into sync and daemon paths.
Nix-first documentation conflicts with legacy onboarding material.
CI omits maintained integration suites and does not fail link checking.
Credential tools are separate from the home-sync package.
Managed files are declared in Home Manager while mutable environment and credentials stay out of the Nix store.
Gitleaks, local structural hooks, read-only permissions, and pinned action revisions protect the development boundary.
Credential retrieval output is a trust boundary because it can be emitted to stdout or clipboard.
Keychain ACLs, effective store permissions, and remote authorization cannot be verified from the snapshot.
Repository directories define the main architectural boundaries.
Conventional home files and public commands have deterministic mappings.
Home-sync exposes CLI operations and orchestrates Git synchronization.
Effective home-sync behavior is Git repository synchronization rather than generic configuration synchronization.
The repository creates a Nix-first Unix home environment with shell, credential, Git, package, and sync tools.
The flake offers standalone Home Manager and nix-darwin configurations using one shared home module.
The system is a hybrid layered architecture with declarative ownership, convention linking, and mutable operational state.
Nix, Bash/Zsh, and Python are primary implementation technologies; home-sync requires Python 3.11 or later.
Nixpkgs, nix-darwin, and Home Manager are reproducible configuration inputs.
GitHub Actions and the listed test and quality tools are configured.
Bats exercises script workflows and pytest exercises home-sync.
Home-sync test quality uses coverage and metrics mutation testing in CI.
